records.reason: A polar bromo carboxylic-acid anchor at high PE/EA probes whether donor and acid interactions create a delayed completion tail beyond ordinary aromatic baselines.
A weakly polar aromatic ketone at zero PE/EA provides a low-retention baseline point for separating ordinary carbonyl behavior from polar-tail corrections.
The amino-nitrile scaffold has a broad predicted V1/V2 interval at 5/1, making it useful for nitrogen-specific endpoint calibration.
A high-ratio anisole derivative tests whether ordinary ether-rich aromatic chemistry extrapolates smoothly into late-solvent conditions.
This narrow-forecast dimethoxy brominated aromatic is a neutral control for calibrating ordinary aromatic representation beside high-tail experiments.
An aromatic aldehyde at 1/1 adds moderate-polarity carbonyl coverage and tests aldehyde transfer across substitution patterns.
A dibromo aldehyde at high PE/EA tests halogenated carbonyl transfer and possible endpoint broadening from increased aromatic mass.
A molecule-novel methyl benzonitrile-like row supplies a compact weakly polar anchor for neutral aromatic generalization.
A donor-containing phenol at zero PE/EA supplies the weak-strength end of a donor response curve and tests scaffold-specific retention.
A halogenated aldehyde at 1/1 provides an intermediate carbonyl/halogen anchor for distinguishing ordinary aromatic retention from multifunctional tails.
Methoxybenzene at 10/1 adds baseline condition coverage for a common weakly polar ether scaffold.
A chlorinated alkylbenzene at 1/1 is a compact neutral transfer point for separating halogen and alkyl effects from polarity.
A simple bromoalkylbenzene at 10/1 provides a low-polarity condition control for hydrophobic structural transfer.
This molecule-novel diarylethene-like anchor expands neutral aromatic coverage and tests for overcorrection after polar-tail repair.
A second low-strength phenol point at 1/1 complements the zero-PE/EA phenol experiment and probes the onset of donor-driven retention.
A weakly polar high-mass aryl iodide provides a molecular-weight and halogen anchor without donor interactions.
A high-ratio fused aromatic point has a broad predicted interval and tests whether aromaticity alone can generate a long completion tail.
A biphenyl-like neutral scaffold at 1/1 and higher loading supplies a loading baseline for nonpolar aromatic chemistry.
A brominated anisole at zero PE/EA and high loading tests whether amount affects a weakly polar aromatic scaffold.
The same biphenyl-like scaffold at lower loading forms a direct loading contrast and can distinguish amount shifts from structural effects.
A donor-containing heteroaromatic aldehyde at 10/1 has a broad forecast and probes endpoint-specific V2 behavior from combined oxygen and aldehyde functionality.
A diaryl sulfone-like scaffold at 2/1 targets a moderately polar high-width region and tests strong acceptor interactions without donors.
A sulfur-containing heteroaromatic at 2/1 is a low-width heteroatom-transfer control distinct from oxygen- and nitrogen-rich chemistry.
The methylpyridine-like scaffold has a very broad predicted interval at 10/1, making it valuable for nitrogen-mediated late-retention calibration.
A multifunctional ester-ketone at zero PE/EA supplies a low-strength point for a carbonyl-rich scaffold with uncertain endpoint width.
A dimethoxy dibrominated aromatic at 5/1 tests ordinary ether and halogen transfer in a moderately uncertain region.
A dialdehyde scaffold at 5/1 has a broad predicted V2 interval and probes whether multiple carbonyls broaden completion independently of onset.
A bromobenzonitrile at 10/1 supplies a nitrile and halogen control for acceptor effects without a donor.
A multifunctional aromatic ketone at 5/1 provides an intermediate carbonyl-rich point for endpoint calibration against more strongly polar scaffolds.
A donor-containing fused aromatic alcohol at zero PE/EA tests whether one donor on a larger scaffold produces a broad tail or remains near an ordinary alcohol baseline.
A bromoacetate at 2/1 is a compact multifunctional control for ester and halogen effects in the lower-retention region.
An oxime-like donor and acceptor scaffold at 1/1 provides a polar comparison point for functional-group arrangement effects without relying on a generic polarity correction.

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback reinforced that V2 errors are localized in multifunctional, donor-containing, nitrogen-rich, and conjugated scaffolds, while neutral aromatic rows form a much larger baseline region that needs protection from overcorrection. The batch therefore combines high-width polar and carbonyl-rich probes with weakly polar, halogenated, sulfur-containing, and neutral aromatic controls. Loading and condition variation are included where they can distinguish structural effects from amount or solvent response.
batch_rationale: The batch covers several chemical regimes and predicted failure regions rather than concentrating only on the largest forecast values. Polar and multifunctional rows target endpoint-tail repair; neutral and weakly polar anchors constrain transfer across the broader catalog; and multiple loading or condition contrasts test whether onset and completion respond independently. This combination should improve the retrained model's V1/V2 generalization across both high-retention tail rows and ordinary aromatic rows.
